title: Investigate & fix slab-shredding GPU OOM with cache tombstone amplification
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Multiple customers across Hosted and Dedicated reported sudden GPU OOM spikes correlated with long-running transformer sessions. Investigation shows allocator slab churn timed with an aggressive KV cache tombstone growth heuristic; together they cause transient slab shredding and OOM cascades on 48GB+ nodes. This ticket tracks triage, a short-term mitigation rollout, and a runtime patch to eliminate the amplification mode.
steps_to_reproduce: Simulate long-lived chat sessions with heavy prefix caching and many small ephemeral keys (mix of 64B and 8KB entries)
Use hosted workload profile: requests with varied sequence lengths and intermittent batching bursts
Observe memory usage: allocator slab churn correlates with KV tombstone sweeps and sudden rise in peak resident GPU memory leading to OOM within 2-5 minutes
investigation_notes: 2025-01-18: Pager received from customer ACME-ML (hosted) showing repeated OOMs on g4dn-48. Logs indicate frequent tombstone accumulation in KV index followed by slab allocation failures.
2025-01-19: Reproduced locally using workload-sim v2 with prefix caching enabled; heap histogram shows fragmentation rising before OOM.

2025-01-20: Heap profiling traced to allocator free path where alternating small/large allocations create interleaved free lists (slab-shredding). Concurrent tombstone compaction increased allocation pressure momentarily, amplifying fragmentation.

2025-01-21: Confirmed race between async tombstone compactor and session evictor: compactor spike causes transient peak allocations due to region reclaims, followed by failed coalescing because free-runner pointers were invalidated by a preceding evict.
root_cause: A timing-dependent interaction: aggressive KV tombstone compaction ran concurrently with session eviction leading to non-coalesced free runs (slab shredding). The allocator's current coalescing heuristic assumed single-threaded reclaim; under concurrent compactions, fragmentation temporarily prevents large contiguous allocations causing GPU OOMs.
short_term_mitigation: 2025-01-20: Rollout - temporarily disable background tombstone compaction on Hosted control plane for affected clusters (canary -> global over 3 hours)
Throttle session-evictor concurrency to 1 per-GPU on Dedicated clusters to reduce interleaved frees
Add emergency autoscaling policy: proactively shift traffic to lower-util nodes when fragmentation metric > 0.6
long_term_fix_summary: Introduce allocator-level synchronized coalescer for tombstone-driven frees and change compactor to use staged, fixed-size reclamation windows that avoid mass concurrent free activities. Add a fragmentation-aware placement heuristic to the runtime kernel selection so large contiguous allocations prefer low-fragment arenas.
work_items: Implement allocator coalescer lock-free rendezvous and unit tests (ENG-902468-A)
Refactor tombstone compactor: staged windows with backoff and soft-quota (ENG-902468-B)
Add instrumentation: fragmentation live metric, percent-coalesced, tombstone-sweep-latency (ENG-902468-C)
Run 48h soak on Dedicated canary pool and validate with synthetic high-prefix workload (ENG-902468-D)
Prepare rollback and customer communication playbook (support runbook update)
implementation_notes: Allocator patch implements a rendezvous epoch for compaction frees; uses per-arena sequencing token to ensure coalescing is applied before concurrent evictors mutate free lists.
Compactor now limits contiguous reclaimed bytes to 64MB per window and yields for 200ms between windows; tuned after microbench.
Added a metric 'runtime.fragmentation_ratio' exposed in console; threshold 0.55 triggers autoscaling suggestion in Optimize recommendations
testing_plan: Unit tests for allocator coalescer under simulated concurrency (deterministic scheduler)
Integration soak: 72-hour run with mixed sequence lengths and cache churn on canary nodes
Performance regression tests for token latency with new compactor windows (ensure <5% p95 token latency regression)
Chaos test: interleave compactor, evictor, and workload bursts with fault injection to validate stability
rollout_plan: Canary: dedicate 2 nodes in eu-west-1 (hosted) and 1 Dedicated pool for 48h with increased telemetry
Staged: 25% clusters over 6 hours observing fragmentation and OOM rate
Full: global rollout gated on fragmentation_ratio reduction and zero OOM regressions for 24h
Rollback: revert compactor windows and re-enable tombstone compaction flags if error rate increases

2025-01-22: Follow-up with reproducible timeline, canary schedule, and recommended configuration changes for Dedicated customers (throttle evictor)
Prepare e-mail template and support playbook to send to customers with impacted runs after patch verification
